name: acid.isolation_read_phenomena
behaviors: SET [SESSION] TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL for all four levels and @@transaction_isolation / @@tx_isolation; invalid values rejected (1231 name, 1232 number); SET TRANSACTION without SESSION applies to the next transaction only and is rejected inside one (1568) while SET SESSION inside a transaction is accepted; no dirty read at any level (READ UNCOMMITTED included); non-repeatable read and phantom under READ UNCOMMITTED / READ COMMITTED; none under REPEATABLE READ / SERIALIZABLE, rows deleted after the snapshot stay visible; own writes visible on top of the snapshot; snapshot taken by the first statement, not BEGIN; START TRANSACTION READ ONLY rejects DML (1792); autocommit=0 opens an invisible transaction until COMMIT, ROLLBACK discards it
suspected_bug: START TRANSACTION WITH CONSISTENT SNAPSHOT does not take the snapshot at START: session c2 runs 'set session transaction isolation level repeatable read; start transaction with consistent snapshot;', c1 then commits 'update iso_t set v = 151 where id = 1', and c2's first 'select v from iso_t where id = 1' returns 151 (MySQL returns the value from before the update); the snapshot is only fixed by that first read (a later committed update to 152 is not seen)
note: Two connections with an explicit statement order; nothing depends on timing. READ UNCOMMITTED is accepted but never shows uncommitted data (MVCC), recorded as behavior rather than a bug.

name: acid.write_conflicts
behaviors: READ COMMITTED lost update with literal writes (later writer wins, both commit); v = v + n waits for the row lock and re-reads (no lost update); READ COMMITTED SELECT ... FOR UPDATE returns the latest committed row; first-updater-wins under REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE: UPDATE or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE of a row changed after the snapshot fails with 6235 'can't serialize access for this transaction', only the statement is rolled back and the transaction commits its other writes; if the first updater rolls back the waiter succeeds; rows inserted after a REPEATABLE READ snapshot are not returned by FOR UPDATE nor touched by UPDATE without WHERE (affected rows 3), a row deleted after the snapshot makes both fail with 6235; write skew succeeds under SERIALIZABLE and REPEATABLE READ; a concurrent INSERT of the same key waits, then 1062 if the first inserter commits or success if it rolls back
suspected_bug: SERIALIZABLE is snapshot isolation and allows write skew: two SERIALIZABLE transactions both read 'select sum(on_call) from wc_oncall' = 2, one runs 'update wc_oncall set on_call = 0 where doctor = 'alice'', the other '... where doctor = 'bob'', both COMMIT succeed and the sum becomes 0 (ANSI / MySQL SERIALIZABLE would block or fail one of them); probably by design (Oracle-style) but it deviates from MySQL
note: Blocking statements are sent with send, given --exec sleep 1 to reach their lock wait, then reaped after the other session ends; every expected value is the same whether or not the statement had started waiting.

name: acid.row_locks
behaviors: row lock held by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / UPDATE / DELETE: FOR UPDATE NOWAIT, NO_WAIT and WAIT 1 fail with 1205 'Lock wait timeout exceeded; try restarting transaction'; FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED returns (and locks) the other rows; non-locking reads never block and see the committed row; ob_trx_lock_timeout (microseconds) bounds UPDATE / DELETE / INSERT / FOR UPDATE waits with 1205, rolling back only that statement; new keys and other rows are not blocked; LOCK IN SHARE MODE conflicts with FOR UPDATE, UPDATE and another LOCK IN SHARE MODE; locks are released at COMMIT and ROLLBACK; innodb_lock_wait_timeout is a mock (SET gives warning 1235, value stays 50)
suspected_bug: LOCK IN SHARE MODE takes an exclusive row lock: after c1 'select * from rl_t where id = 2 lock in share mode', c2 'select * from rl_t where id = 2 lock in share mode' (ob_trx_lock_timeout = 1000000) fails with 1205 (MySQL lets two share-mode readers coexist); 'set session innodb_lock_wait_timeout = 1' only returns Warning 1235 'This system variable now is mock not supported' and the value stays 50, so the MySQL way of bounding lock waits has no effect
note: Gray area: uses the public ob_ system variable ob_trx_lock_timeout (listed in ob_system_variable_init.json) as the public equivalent of innodb_lock_wait_timeout. The 1-second lock timeouts are the assertions; everything else is an explicit statement order.

name: fork.merge_strategies
behaviors: MERGE TABLE incoming INTO current [STRATEGY FAIL|THEIRS|OURS] is a two-way merge keyed on the primary key with no merge base: incoming-only keys are inserted under every strategy (re-inserting rows current deleted), current-only keys are kept (incoming deletes never propagate), a key whose non-key columns differ (NULL-safe <=>, column collation) is a conflict whichever side changed it, identical changes are not; FAIL (the default) applies nothing and fails 4179 'MERGE TABLE: <n> conflict(s) detected. Use THEIRS or OURS strategy to resolve. FAIL strategy is not allowed', and applies the inserts when there is no conflict; THEIRS overwrites conflicts with incoming values, OURS keeps current; affected rows = inserts + updates; MERGE joins an explicit transaction (ROLLBACK undoes it); generated columns compared but recomputed; MERGE of a table into itself is a no-op; unknown strategy 1064; DIFF TABLE after each merge
suspected_bug: (1) Case-only changes are lost under the default collation: after 'fork table mg_base to mg_inc; update mg_inc set v = 'TEN' where id = 10; ... merge table mg_inc into mg_theirs strategy theirs;' mg_theirs keeps v = 'ten' and DIFF TABLE does not list id 10, because utf8mb4_general_ci compares 'ten' <=> 'TEN' as equal (with a utf8mb4_bin column the same change is a conflict and THEIRS applies it); this is the brief's 'keeps b, adds row 4' observation. (2) MERGE reports 'affected rows: 7' to the client but 'select row_count()' right after returns 0. (3) Without a merge base THEIRS also reverts rows only current changed (id 1 'one-cur' -> 'one') and deletes on either side are never merged (design, listed for review).
note: Copies of the current table are made with FORK TABLE after the current-side changes, one per strategy, so all strategies start from the same state.

name: fork.diff_table
behaviors: DIFF TABLE current AGAINST incoming result shape: columns __table, __flag, primary-key columns in table column order (not PRIMARY KEY order), then the other columns; __table is the qualified 'db.table'; one row per key present on one side, two rows per key whose values differ, nothing for equal rows, empty result for identical tables; rows ordered by primary-key columns then __table, so a AGAINST b equals b AGAINST a; NULL-safe comparison with column semantics (JSON by value, DECIMAL 1.50 = 1.5, trailing spaces and case ignored under utf8mb4_general_ci, VARBINARY and DOUBLE exact); key-only tables; cross-database and implied-database names; the session's uncommitted changes are included; ORGANIZATION HEAP tables with a primary key; LONGTEXT values
suspected_bug: __flag is the constant 'INSERT' for every row, whatever the difference: e.g. after 'delete from df_b where a = 3 and b = 'a'' the deleted row shows as 'test.df_a INSERT 3 a q 4', and both versions of a modified row are flagged INSERT, so the column carries no information
note: LONGTEXT runs are masked with --replace_regex (the values are 100000 characters long).

name: fork.merge_diff_errors
behaviors: DIFF / MERGE need a primary key (1235 'DIFF TABLE on table without primary key not supported' / 'MERGE TABLE on table without primary key not supported'); any visible column-definition mismatch (count, order, name, length, nullability, default, key membership, a view on either side) fails with 4029 'Schema error'; a missing table or database fails with 1146 'Table doesn't exist'; MERGE needs SELECT on incoming and SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on current (1142 names the first missing privilege), DIFF needs SELECT on both; column definitions are validated before privileges; MERGE THEIRS replaces a whole LONGTEXT value
suspected_bug: Error texts lose detail: the code formats 'MERGE TABLE requires both tables to have identical column definitions' but the client only gets 'ERROR HY000: Schema error' (4029); 'diff table er_cur against er_missing' returns 'Table doesn't exist' without naming the table; a user without SELECT on er_def gets 'Schema error' from 'diff table er_cur against er_def' instead of 1142, so the schema of a table the user cannot read is probed before the privilege check
note: Creates and drops user er_user through public SQL (CREATE USER / GRANT).

name: fork.fork_database
behaviors: FORK DATABASE copies every base table with data, primary key, unique and secondary indexes, CHECK constraints, generated columns, partitioning and AUTO_INCREMENT position (SHOW CREATE TABLE); foreign keys between tables of the source database (including a self-reference) point into the new database; afterwards both databases are independent (DML, AUTO_INCREMENT) and constraints are enforced in the copy (1452, 1062, 3819, 1451); DIFF TABLE across them; empty database; names lower-cased; errors: unknown source 1049, existing target or source itself 1007, mysql / oceanbase / information_schema 1235, routines (procedure or function), triggers and spatial indexes 1235 with specific texts; a failed fork leaves no target database
suspected_bug: Objects are dropped silently: views are not copied (no error or warning; 'select * from fdb_dst.v' fails 1146) and a foreign key to a table in another database is not recreated (fdb_dst.x accepts 'insert into fdb_dst.x values (2, 99)' while fdb_src.x rejects it with 1452)
note: No existing judge case covers FORK DATABASE (fork_database_check_names is not in the manifest).

name: vector.exact_distance
behaviors: values of l2_distance, l2_squared, l1_distance, cosine_distance (NULL for a zero vector), inner_product, negative_inner_product, vector_distance (default EUCLIDEAN, MANHATTAN, COSINE, DOT), vector_dims, vector_norm on literals and VECTOR columns; NULL arguments give NULL; element-wise + - *; VECTOR printing (shortest float32 form, no spaces); errors 7600 'Invalid dimension for vector.' / 'inconsistent dimension: expected 3 got 2', 3140 'Invalid JSON text.', 1210 'Invalid argument'; exact top-k without an index for every distance, NULL distances first, DESC ordering, ties broken by id, distances rounded to 6 decimals

name: vector.hnsw_topk
behaviors: HNSW / HNSW_SQ / HNSW_BQ indexes with l2, inner_product and cosine; SHOW CREATE TABLE defaults (M=16, EF_CONSTRUCTION=200, EF_SEARCH=64, REFINE_TYPE=SQ8, BQ_USE_FHT=TRUE); APPROXIMATE / APPROX top-k equals the exact top-k (ids, order, distances) for l2_distance, l2_squared, negative_inner_product and cosine_distance; PARAMETERS(ef_search=n); OFFSET; inner_product DESC APPROX and a mismatched distance function fall back to the exact answer; filtered top-k with WHERE; rows with a NULL vector are never returned by APPROXIMATE (an exact ORDER BY sorts them first); INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE and the session's own uncommitted insert are visible, ROLLBACK removes it; errors: APPROX without LIMIT 1064, two ORDER BY items 1235, FOR UPDATE 1235
note: Dataset chosen so that no two rows tie for any query (pairwise distinct distances); with 16 rows and the default ef_search 64 every HNSW search visits the whole graph, so approximate and exact answers coincide.

name: vector.ivf_topk
behaviors: IVF_FLAT with l2, inner_product and cosine, created inline on an empty table or with CREATE VECTOR INDEX on populated tables; SHOW CREATE TABLE defaults (LIB=OB, SAMPLE_PER_NLIST=256, NBITS=8 for IVF_PQ); with nlist <= ob_ivf_nprobes (default 8) APPROXIMATE equals exact, also with WHERE and after INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE; NULL vectors never returned; IVF_SQ8 built on existing rows ranks by quantized distance (top 4 exact, ranks 5 and 6 swapped); IVF parameter errors 1235 (M on IVF_FLAT, M not dividing the dimension, EF_SEARCH on IVF, NLIST 0 or 65537, LIB=VSAG)
suspected_bug: IVF_SQ8 created on an empty table never ranks by distance: 'create table ivf_sq8_empty(id int primary key, v vector(4), vector index vidx(v) with (distance=l2, type=ivf_sq8, nlist=3)); insert into ivf_sq8_empty select id, v from ivf_src;' then 'select id, round(l2_distance(v, '[2,12,8,1]'), 6) d from ivf_sq8_empty order by l2_distance(v, '[2,12,8,1]') approx limit 3' returns ids 2, 3, 1 (16.911535, 6.244998, 14.560220) while the exact top 3 is 14, 3, 7
note: IVF_PQ result order depends on randomly seeded k-means codebooks and is not asserted (only its DDL and row count). Every list is probed (nlist 2 or 3 <= 8), so IVF_FLAT answers do not depend on the random centroids; the IVF_SQ8 rankings were identical across repeated exploratory runs with different k-means seeds. Gray area: reads the public ob_ system variable ob_ivf_nprobes (default 8) without changing it.

name: vector.sparse_sindi
behaviors: SPARSEVECTOR literals (whitespace accepted, keys printed sorted without spaces, 1.0 printed as 1, '{}' empty, a repeated key keeps the last value) and 1210 errors with specific texts for bad literals; inner_product / negative_inner_product (0 when no dimension is shared), vector_dims counts entries; l2_distance / cosine_distance 5083 and vector_norm 1210 even on an empty table; SINDI index DDL (SHOW CREATE TABLE) and 1235 for DISTANCE=L2, TYPE=HNSW on sparse and SINDI on dense; APPROXIMATE top-k equals the exact top-k among rows sharing a dimension with the query, zero-score and NULL rows never returned ('{9:1}' and '{}' queries return no rows while the exact query returns zero-score rows); WHERE filters and DML reflected immediately

name: fts.tokenize_parsers
behaviors: TOKENIZE() token sets per parser: space (default; word chars letters / digits / _, lower-cased, 3..84 characters, built-in stopwords, a CJK run is one token), beng (punctuation splits), ngram (ngram_token_size), ngram2 (min / max_ngram_size), ik (smart and max_word); {"output": "all"} counts and doc_len; NULL / '' give []; parser name case- and space-insensitive; additional_args validation; errors 1582 argument count, 1128 unknown parser, 1210 empty parser / out-of-range sizes / unknown option, 1235 case / stopwords / foreign property, 3141 invalid JSON
note: Arrays are unpacked with JSON_TABLE and sorted, so only token sets are asserted; the raw (hash-map) order is pinned separately in fts.tokenize_raw_order. The 1235 message for the case option reads 'case indentifier not supported' (typo in the original, reproduced as is).

name: fts.tokenize_raw_order
behaviors: exact JSON text of TOKENIZE() for space, ngram, ngram2, beng and ik, default and {"output": "all"}: token order inside the array (the tokenizer's hash-map iteration order, neither text order nor sorted) and JSON formatting
note: Kept apart from fts.tokenize_parsers so a port that reproduces the token sets but not this order fails only here; a human should decide whether the order is part of the contract.

name: fts.match_modes
behaviors: default space parser and its SHOW CREATE TABLE properties; natural-language MATCH: matching rows and BM25 relevance (6 decimals), repeated query words count once, case-insensitive, stopwords and short words dropped ('and' is not a stopword), 0 for non-matching rows and NULL documents, WHERE MATCH without ORDER BY sorted by relevance; boolean mode +, -, (), bare terms, only -terms match nothing, double quotes ignored, * ~ < > @ are syntax errors 1149; IN MATCH PHRASE MODE (adjacent, in order); WITH QUERY EXPANSION 1235; no matching index 1191; non-constant AGAINST 1064; two-column index, columns in either order; INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE reflected
suspected_bug: The BM25 document count is frozen into the cached plan: 'select id, round(match(body) against('alpha'), 6) s from fm_pc where match(body) against('alpha') order by s desc, id' returns 0.371622 for ids 1 and 2 with 4 rows, still 0.371622 after 6 more non-matching rows are inserted (stale count 4), while the same query with 'limit 5' appended returns 1.819126 (count 10). Also: double quotes in boolean mode are silently ignored, so '"text search"' matches any row with either word.
note: Rows are freshly inserted and never compacted, so N, df and avgdl (10) are exact and every relevance value is reproducible. Statement texts are kept distinct wherever fresh statistics are expected.

name: fts.parser_indexes
behaviors: FULLTEXT indexes WITH PARSER ngram / ngram2 / beng / ik with PARSER_PROPERTIES, inline and with CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX on a populated table, SHOW CREATE TABLE properties; natural-language MATCH splits the query with the index parser (ngram substrings and CJK words, ngram2 2..4-grams, beng punctuation and min_token_size, ik max_word segmentation) with relevance values; boolean-mode terms are not split by the parser (ngram(2): 'el' matches, 'ello' does not; ngram2(2..4): 'ello' matches, 'hello' does not; ngram(3) index built later: 'llo' matches, 'll' does not); '@' in boolean mode 1149; errors 1128 unknown parser, 1210 out-of-range / max < min / bad ik_mode, 1235 property of another parser, 1064 empty or negative property
suspected_bug: Boolean mode and natural-language mode disagree on the same index: on an ngram(2) index 'match(body) against('ello')' finds rows 1 and 2 but 'match(body) against('ello' in boolean mode)' finds nothing, because boolean terms bypass the index parser

name: hybrid.search_fusion
behaviors: DBMS_HYBRID_SEARCH.GET_SQL text for match, knn, weighted hybrid and RRF hybrid requests (defaults and explicit rank_constant, rank_window_size, size, from, _source); SEARCH JSON hits (_source columns plus _score, keys ordered by length, knn score round(1/(1+l2), 8), NULL when nothing matches); weighted fusion = BM25 + vector score; RRF = 1/(keyword_rank + c) + 1/(semantic_rank + c), c = 60 by default, 4-decimal DECIMAL terms, one term for one-sided hits, ties by insertion order; size / from paging, knn limited to min(k, size); boost; the generated SQL run directly returns the same ranking; rank ignored without both query and knn; DML visible to the next search; a user PRIMARY KEY table fails 1235 'table with user provided primary key not supported' unless ORGANIZATION HEAP (with SYNC_MODE=IMMEDIATE on the vector index)
note: BM25 scores are full doubles in the JSON, so those hits are unpacked with JSON_TABLE (ordinality keeps the hit order) and rounded to 6 decimals; vector-only, 0/1 and RRF scores are exact and shown raw. A heap table's vector index defaults to SYNC_MODE=ASYNC, so a search right after INSERT can miss rows (seen while exploring); the scenario uses SYNC_MODE=IMMEDIATE and never relies on async catch-up.

name: hybrid.query_dsl
behaviors: GET_SQL text and SEARCH hits for term, terms (boost), range, bool must / should / filter / must_not (filter-only scores 0, union_merge hint for two matches on one index), multi_match and query_string (field^2) queries; relaxed JSON accepted; knn filter, similarity (distance threshold after top-k), boost and arrays of knn clauses (scores summed); vector score formulas for l2, cosine (1 - d/2) and inner_product; GET_SQL of '{}'; errors with codes and texts: 1210, 3140, 5453, 1149, 1235, 1146 (names the table), 1103, 3064, 4182, 1708, 1191 (SEARCH only, GET_SQL succeeds), 1210 for knn on a non-vector column
suspected_bug: Upper-case top-level keys are silently ignored instead of rejected: '{query: {match: {body: "data"}}, _source: ["id"], SIZE: 1,}' returns 2 hits (SIZE dropped without error) while an unknown lower-case key such as "bogus" fails with 1149
note: Hits whose order is not defined by an ORDER BY (similarity, multi-knn ties) are unpacked with JSON_TABLE and sorted by id.

name: hybrid.es_mode_partitions
behaviors: es_mode: true / "true" rewrites top-level match, multi_match and query_string into ES-style MATCH(`col`^w, ..., 'text', 'operator=or;boost=..[;minimum_should_match=n];type=best_fields') with score() (GET_SQL text and SEARCH hits), term queries unchanged, es_mode inside a hybrid request; es_mode "maybe" 1210, numeric 3064; es_mode changes multi_match scores (field weight inside MATCH); ES-style MATCH / score() in plain SQL: best_fields vs most_fields, field weights and boost multiply BM25, minimum_should_match=n; errors 1235 for score() outside an ES-style MATCH ('The position of score() is not supported'), score() inside an expression ('no score expr is not supported'), operator=and, type=cross_fields / phrase; 1064 without the options argument or without ^w; HASH-partitioned table: GET_SQL adds `_part_col_0` and joins on it, SEARCH match / knn / RRF hits, DML visible
suspected_bug: Unknown option keys in the ES-style MATCH options string are silently ignored: 'select id, score() s from hm_docs where match(body^1, 'search', 'bogus=1') order by s desc, id' succeeds with the default options instead of failing; the 'operator=and' error text has a double space ('match operator 'and'  not supported')
note: Plain-SQL score() values cannot be wrapped in round() (that is itself an asserted error), so they are shown with --replace_numeric_round 6.
